subtopic: Target Date Funds as 401(k) Default Investments
source_evidence: Some 401(k) plans use these funds as the default investment for plan participants who have not selected their investments under the plan.
answer: Target date funds may be used as default investments in some 401(k) plans. This means a plan may place participants who have not selected their own investments into a target date fund. These funds hold a mix of investments and are designed to shift toward a more conservative mix as the target date approaches. A fund’s target date retirement year generally refers to the year the investor expects to retire.
